outcomes: Evaluate basic grammar and writing mechanics resulting in well-crafted sentences
Write a well-organized paragraph
Write clear sentences that demonstrate proficiency with grammar, mechanics, and usage

outcomes: Apply proper communication styles to improve personal communication
Outline obtainable goals and personal strengths and weaknesses
Identify the warning signs and apply coping strategies to negative behaviors/emotions

outcomes: Conduct literary research to write a formal essay.
Apply knowledge of advanced math including fractions, percentages, charts, graphs, and algebra concepts to solve problems.
Define and apply concepts within natural science and social studies

rows.title: Managerial Accounting

outcomes: Calculate the estimated cost of a product or a service.
Using contribution margin, calculate sales to achieve break-even and target profit.
Prepare budgets used to plan and control an organization.

rows.title: Intermediate Income Taxes - Partnerships and LLCs
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Prepare a basic Federal income tax return for partnerships.
Conduct research on topics and changes of the Federal income tax rules.
Identify the filing and payment requirements of a U.S. partnership.

outcomes: Calculate the cost of a product or a service provided including overhead using both traditional and activity-based allocation.
Calculate contribution margin and be able to estimate cost, volume, profit analysis and how it is used to predict revenues and costs of an organization.
Prepare budgets used to plan and control an organization.

rows.title: Auditing
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Understand generally accepted auditing standards, audit reporting, and the theory and methodology of auditing.
Distinguish the three different components of audit risk.
Identify various circumstances in which the standard report must be modified.
Show understanding and explain the ethical and professional standards of an auditor.

rows.title: Introduction to Biological Anthropology
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Students will critically examine and evaluate issues in human genetics, non-human primate morphology and behavior, human evolution, and human diversity.
Students will demonstrate the use of the scientific method as a tool for problem solving.
Students will analyze four key areas in physical anthropology to identify the place of humans in relation to other species.
Students will formulate how we as a single human species have evolved from a common ancestor.
Students will recognize the impact that cultural variation has on perceptions of human biology.

rows.title: Honors Language and Culture
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate a broad knowledge of the global world through understanding of other languages and cultures.
Evaluate how language can create and neutralize biases which may be present regarding dialects, other languages, multiculturalism, and multilingualism.
Apply and utilize a descriptive value-neutral approach to language and culture rather than a prescriptive one.

Demonstrate the capacity to make informed ethical choices regarding professional application of the material of this discipline e.g., Speech Pathology, field methods, teaching, develop a commitment to accurate work, e.g., phonetic evaluation for speech pathologists.
*Demonstrate a higher level of critical thinking and professionalism in presentations.

rows.title: Apprenticeship Child Growth and Development (DS1)

rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Explain children's development from conception through adolescence in the physical, social, emotional, and cognitive domains.
Identify cultural, economic, political, and historical contexts that impact children's development.
Apply knowledge of development and major theoretical frameworks to child observations, child abuse, and milestones.

outcomes: Describe strategies used to promote the health, safety, and nutrition of children and adults in early childhood settings.

Identify regulations, standards, policies, and procedures related to health, safety, and nutrition in care and education settings.

Demonstrate the skills of a professional teacher including effective communication, ethical practice, responsibilities to children and families, and commitment to ongoing professional development.

Demonstrate proficiency in the effective use of educational technology which promotes 21st century skills.

Synthesize and summarize indigenous and non-indigenous art philosophies of Africa, Oceania, and Native North American cultures.
Compare and contrast works of art and architecture in terms of their media, formal elements, subject matter and iconography, and cultural and historical context.

Execute a historical and contextual analysis of works of contemporary art.
Identify contemporary works of art and architecture to their wider historical context.

Demonstrate a basic level understanding of creating the visual illusion of space in a two-dimensional drawing composition.

Create the illusion of volume and space in pastel drawing.

Create original mural projects that apply an understanding of design principles.

outcomes: Identify and utilize intermediate-level elements/principles of art and design in figure drawing works of art.
Create a proportional contour drawing of the human figure at an intermediate level.
Apply an intermediate-level working knowledge of the human skeleton, muscle structure, human anatomy, and anatomical proportion as it applies to figure drawing.

rows.title: Intermediate Illustration

rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Compose their Illustrations using a more advanced level of the sequential design process (thumbnail sketches, pencil roughs, color roughs, final works, to post-production.)
Demonstrate the ability to draw the human anatomical form accurately by using traditional and/ or non-traditional media.
Utilize a more advanced verbal analysis to work presented in the class within the context of a class critique.
Develop an individual illustrative creative style through assigned personal projects approved by instructor.

outcomes: properly and accurately locate and identify Asian nations.
analyze and articulate core concepts of Ethnic Studies, including but not limited to race and ethnicity, racialization, equity, ethnocentrism, Eurocentrism, and White supremacy.

rows.title: Honors American Sign Language II

rows.title: Introduction to the Solar System

outcomes: Identify the accomplishments of a diverse set of historical and contemporary astronomers.
Explain the lunar phases and the motions of the night sky.
Identify key developments from the history of astronomy, including human space exploration.
Describe how the Solar System formed.

Explain the empirical evidence used to justify the modern understanding of the Solar System.

rows.title: Principles and Procedures in the Criminal Justice System

rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Explain and evaluate legal concepts of due process within the criminal justice system.
Analyze and evaluate the stages and functions of the criminal justice trial process.

rows.title: Street Gangs
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Identify and examine primary factors leading youth to join gangs.
Identify primary CA Penal Code sections that address gangs.

rows.title: Organized Crime
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Identify the major types of criminal activities organized crime perpetrates.
Identify and explain US investigative efforts towards organized crime.

rows.title: Introduction to Drone Laws
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Evaluate first-responder drone law issues and understand the basics of how to respond in the field.

rows.title: Work Experience - IT Cybersecurity and Computing
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Develop short term goals related to the skills they are developing in the work environment.
Apply new career skills through practical experience in the work environment.

rows.title: Python Programming
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate writing Python programs.
Demonstrate using the IF block structure.
Demonstrate using loops and methods.

rows.title: Introduction to Programming
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Write computer programs utilizing programming language syntax elements including basic control structures and non-recursive functions.
Write computer programs utilizing native and array-based data types, including constant and reference type modifiers.
Design and document nontrivial computer programs in an hierarchical manner and in phases (software life cycle).
Write readable computer programs utilizing professional coding standards for identifiers, indentations, spacing and comments.

rows.title: Introduction to Computer Organization
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Apply numeric bases to generation and translation of computer data-type representations.
Demonstrate basic understanding of logic-gate circuitry and Karnaugh Maps, and their use in implementing Von Neuman computer components such as CPUs, ALUs, data channels, and memory.

Describe the layers of computer programming levels including microcode, instruction-set archetecture, assembly, and high-level languages, their relationship to translation tools such as assemblers, compilers, and formal language definition/recognition using finite-state automata.
Describe the relationship between the operating system, processes, and storage, including scheduling, paging and virtual memory, and interrupt-level OS services.

rows.title: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Identify common networking hardware devices, network configuration concepts, and protocols.
Design, install, configure, upgrade, maintain, support, and troubleshoot internetworking devices in a computer network.
Explain important concepts in networking, such as TCP/IP, Ethernet, wireless transmission, virtual networks, and security, and troubleshooting.
Demonstrate appropriate use of command-line tools and software to assess and diagnose the network configuration and security posture of an organization.
Apply security best practices to secure network resources on SOHO and enterprise networks.

rows.title: A+ Essentials Software
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate to use appropriate Microsoft and Linux command line and GUI tools, operating system features, and best practices.
Demonstrate to troubleshoot Microsoft Windows OS, Linux, mobile OS problems and resolve PC security and application issues.
Configure Microsoft Windows and Linux networking on a client/desktop.
Apply security best practices to secure a workstation and the organization from threats and malware on SOHO wireless and wired networks.

rows.title: Microsoft Access
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Design, create and secure Access databases.
Design, create and manage Access tables, relationships, keys and constraints.
Design, create and manage queries in extracting  data from tables.
Design, manage and produce graphical user interface (GUI) using Access Forms.
Design, manage and produce basic to advanced reports.

rows.title: CompTIA Security+ Guide to Network Security
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Identify, detect, and address various types of compromise and security incidents.
Analyze indicators of compromise and determine the type of malware.
Implement secure network architecture concepts, secure systems design, and secure identity and access controls.

rows.title: Windows Server Operating System
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate how to install and configure a server.
Demonstrate how to design different protocols.
Demonstrate how to use the command prompt.

rows.title: Introduction to Intercultural Communication
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Create solutions to address intercultural communication challenges.
Identify values, norms, beliefs and practices across various cultures.
Apply various intercultural communication theories.

rows.title: Group Dynamics
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Employ organizational patterns of informative and persuasive messages relevant to specific audiences, contexts, and occasions
Identify appropriate group communication techniques for specific group situations.
Identify the influences of and communication strategies for ethnic, cultural, generational, gender, and personality diversity.
Identify the strengths and weaknesses of various small group communication theories.
Self-evaluate one's speaking skills of informative and persuasive messages within the team presentation context.

Formulate and present public messages as a team, and evaluate communication effectiveness through research, analysis, and organization of evidence and visual supporting material appropriate for the audience, occasion, and across a variety of contexts.
Select subject matter, approach, and strategy based on analysis of the communication situation, audience, occasion, and purpose.

rows.title: Communication and Conflict Resolution
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Identify conflict management and mediation skills.
Negotiate and mediate conflict in the decision-making process.
Explain the nature of intrapersonal, interpersonal, intragroup, and organizational conflict.

rows.title: Career/Life Planning and Personal Exploration
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Students will be able to express their skills, values, interests, and personality to others and how they relate to their educational and career goals.
Students will be able to identify, research, and evaluate careers that are compatible with their skills, values, interests, and personality.
Students will be able to develop an individualized student education plan demonstrating logical sequencing of courses in order to meet educational goals.

rows.title: Introduction to Social Work and Human Services
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Identify target populations requiring assistance and make recommendations regarding the appropriate social work and human services organization.

Identify and be able to uphold the legal, ethical, and professional practices and responsibilities of working with social work and human services organizations with attention to cultural humility and oppressed groups.
Explain the history and philosophy of the social work and human services profession and assess its role in contemporary society.
Explain the current delivery system environment in which social work and human services client’s needs are addressed.

rows.title: Understanding Child Abuse and Maltreatment
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge of child maltreatment, such as physical abuse, psychological and emotional maltreatment, sexual abuse (intrafamilial and extrafamilial), and neglect (i.e. physical, educational, medical, mental, inadequate supervision etc.).
Demonstrate an understanding of the potential correlations and effect of child maltreatment (i.e. family dynamics, environmental variables etc.).
Demonstrate an understanding of ethical issues regarding both children’s and parents’ rights.
Develop an understanding about one's responsibility as a mandated reporter for child maltreatment reporting.

rows.title: Interpersonal Communication - Honors
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: PART 2:
Apply interpersonal communication theories and research methods to analyze real-world communication scenarios and evaluate their effectiveness.
Analyze the role of communication in shaping personal and social identities, taking into account key factors such as culture, gender, ethnicity, race, age, ability, and sexual orientation.

Evaluate the impact of social and cultural variables (e.g., culture, gender, ethnicity, race, age, accessibility, and orientation) on the initiation, development, and dissolution of interpersonal relationships.
Demonstrate ethical communication practices in interpersonal contexts by identifying ethical dilemmas and applying communication strategies that promote respect, empathy, and integrity.
Identify sources of interpersonal conflict and effectively implement evidence-based conflict management strategies to resolve or mitigate conflict in a variety of relational contexts.

rows.title: Principles of Food Preparation
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Describe food safety and sanitation procedures.
Demonstrate basic knowledge of food preparation terminology and techniques.
Evaluate the sensory attributes of food.

rows.title: Principles of Pantry
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Apply food safety and sanitation practices, including temperature control, safe handling of raw ingredients, and sanitation procedures, particularly in preserving, curing, and preparing cold items.
Demonstrate a variety of items, including basic emulsion sauces and dressings, used in quality salad production.
Identify the fundamentals included in breakfast cookery and sandwich production.
Demonstrate proficiency in preparing cold dishes such as charcuterie, salads, hors d’oeuvres, and breakfast items, using proper garde manger techniques.

Demonstrate professionalism and teamwork in a kitchen environment by developing strong professional habits. This includes punctuality, organization, and effective communication while collaborating with peers to efficiently complete tasks and maintain a positive, cooperative kitchen environment.

rows.title: Introduction to Food & Beverage Management
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate management functions in food and beverage operations.

rows.title: Modern and Sustainable Cuisine
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Explore their history, origins, and use in the modern kitchen.
Identify and utilize seasonal, locally sourced, and sustainable ingredients in their culinary creations, promoting environmental responsibility and supporting the farm-to-table movement.
Evaluate ingredient sourcing with a focus on sustainability, prioritizing local and organic ingredients to support eco-friendly practices and enhance the flavor of dishes.

Evaluate how sustainability practices influence modern culinary trends, including plant-forward cuisine and the farm-to-table movement, while considering their impact on the environment and food industry.
Design and present dishes using modern plating techniques, focusing on balance, aesthetics, and the use of innovative presentation styles to enhance the dining experience.

Demonstrate strong professional habits to demonstrate professionalism and teamwork in a professional kitchen environment. These include punctuality, organization, and effective communication. Collaborate with peers to efficiently complete tasks and maintain a positive, cooperative kitchen environment.

rows.title: Diesel Engines
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate proper safety procedures when working with diesel and CNG engines.
Describe the four stroke cycle, gear and valve train for modern diesel and CNG engines.
Identify the systems, sub-systems, and components on modern diesel and CNG engines.
Analyze, disassembly, and assemble of a diesel or CNG engine.

rows.title: Electrical/Electronic Systems
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate usage of digital multimeter to check voltage, amperage, and resistance.
Define A/C and D/C voltage systems.
Identify microprocessor, sensor, and actuator functions.
Describe multiplexing systems, Control Area Network (CAN-J1939), and logic gates.

rows.title: Introduction to Preventative Maintenance Inspection
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate proper safety procedures when working on medium/heavy-duty vehicles.
Identify engine, air induction, and fuel system in need of maintenance.
Inspect brake components of a medium/heavy-duty vehicle for both air and hydraulic brakes to meet CHP and DOT criteria.
Identify high-voltage components for electric heavy-duty vehicles.

rows.title: History of Film from 1945 to Present
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate comprehension of the history and formulation of motion pictures in both the United States, and internationally, from 1945 to present.
Identify and define key film genre (musicals, westerns, screwball comedies, gangster films, etc.) and formats.
Identify key directors, actors, and films during the time period covered by course, through comparative analysis.

rows.title: Introduction to Video Editing and Postproduction
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Ingest video files into editing software
Operate all basic editing commands in the software
Employ editing decisions in order to produce a coherent video message
Produce content with video/audio levels within professional standards

rows.title: Intermediate Screenwriting for Digital Media
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Identify successful scriptwriting techniques through the viewing of past and current TV episodes and films.
Develop professional creative critiques and discussion points by analyzing other scripts.
Utilize professional techniques of screenwriting structure and dramatic theory to create short film scripts.

rows.title: Work Experience - Digital Media
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Identify three objectives of their work experience course in written form fulfilling the mandated standards of the State of California Education Code Title 5.
Develop short term goals related to the skills they are developing in the work environment.

rows.title: Beginning Audio Production
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Record and mix audio in the studio, for synchronization to video, and in live performance using proper microphone techniques.
Evaluate specific recording, live mixing and synchronization scenarios and apply effective audio production techniques.
Write a plan for a practical recording scenario and explain steps involved in its implementation.

rows.title: Agency Graphic Design Production
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Develop a comprehensive design brief exhibiting advanced-level skills.
Design a comprehensive branding and identity package that incorporates media and design principles.
Create a professional digital portfolio for use in career and educational advancement.
Apply technological and workforce skills to client engagement and services, reflecting the needs of today's online and POS brands.
Manage business operations to meet workforce and client needs.

rows.title: Drone Cinematography & Editing
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Perform basic flight of drone using cinematography techniques to record video
Demonstrate ability to export video content to an editing system and create a cinematic storyline

rows.title: Introduction to Digital Media Arts
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Create unique design solutions.
Use basic tools from industry standard software.
Navigate design software efficiently.
Critique imagery through written and verbal defense of imagery.

rows.title: Advanced Single-Camera/Digital Cinema Production
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Assemble pre-production components for a production on a small-scale and large-scale
Produce and direct an advanced shoot for a single-camera production
Edit two single-camera productions into finished product for a portfolio reel

rows.title: Motion Picture Technical Production
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Create storyboards by breaking a script into scenes.
Demonstrate industry-standard shot composition, audio recording and editing for film.
Prepare a location for technical needs of pre-production.

rows.title: Dance Laboratory III
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Apply critical analysis of performance skills.
Memorize and demonstrate technical and performance dance skills necessary for intermediate level dance projects.

rows.title: Dance as Communication
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Identify movement analysis terminology, nonverbal communication types, and multiple dance intelligences.
Apply movement analysis skills to describe the physical actions of dance.
Utilize various encoding devices as a tool for eliciting, reading, and interpreting the meaning of dance movement.
Analyze and synthesize personal interpretation of dance as communication.

rows.title: Introduction to Modern Dance - I
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate basic fundamental modern dance technique skills.
Interpret and apply basic ballet and modern dance terminology and dance elements to choreographic movement phrases.
Evaluate and self-assess technical dance skills.
Analyze and critique dance elements of choreographic assisgnments, and develop personal expressivity and interpretation of different dances.

rows.title: Dance Concert Performance - III
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate dance concert commitments, expected participation, and the practice and retaining of learned dances.
Execute intermediate level technical and performance skills necessary for small group, duet and/or solo dance role by understanding the choreographer’s intent.
Self-assess intermediate level performance skills to illustrate artistic integrity.

rows.title: Pilates Mat I
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Memorize and identify appropriate Pilates, level I vocabulary to recognize and interpret verbal and written instruction.
Memorize and execute Pilates, level I mat exercises.
Discuss and interpret basic concepts of the Pilates method, level I.
Use critical writing skills to analyze and self-assess one’s own skill set of Pilates, level I mat exercises.

rows.title: Intermediate Mexican Folk Dance I
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Memorize and identify intermediate level Mexican folk-dance vocabulary to recognize and interpret verbal and written instruction.
Demonstrate fundamental technical skills and expressive performance skills appropriate to intermediate level Mexican folk dance.
Use critical writing skills to identify and analyze historical and cultural factors of Mexican folk dance.

rows.title: Conditioning for Dance
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Memorize and identify anatomical vocabulary and basic biomechanics.
Demonstrate basic conditioning exercises.
Use critical writing skills to analyze and identify personal strengths and weaknesses in dance technique.
Apply conditioning exercises to support and enhance dance technique.

rows.title: Introduction to Hip Hop Dance II
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Memorize and identify Hip Hop dance vocabulary to recognize and interpret verbal and written instruction.
Continue to demonstrate technical skills and expressive performance skills appropriate to introductory level Hip Hop dance.
Use critical writing skills to complete personal critique and reflection of a Hip Hop dance performance.
Discuss and interpret fundamental elements of dance composition appropriate to introductory level Hip Hop dance.

rows.title: Salsa Dance I
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Memorize and identify beginning-level salsa dance vocabulary to recognize and interpret verbal and written instruction.
Demonstrate technical skills and expressive performance skills appropriate to beginning-level salsa dance.
Identify historical factors of salsa dance and its influences on other cultures.
Use critical writing skills to analyze and self-assess personal dance techniques.

rows.title: Musical Theatre Dance Techniques II
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate an increased level of technical and performance skills as an ensemble dancer in varied character roles.
Identify the historical and current values of various influential theatrical dance genres, dancers, and choreographers.
Demonstrate the appropriate preparation needed for an ensemble dancing role specified in a musical theatre audition setting.
Design a resume to meet the specific qualifications for a musical dance theatre audition.

rows.title: Ballet II
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Memorize and identify ballet dance vocabulary appropriate to level II to recognize and interpret verbal and written instruction.
Demonstrate technical skills and expressive performance skills appropriate to ballet dance level II.
Use critical writing skills to analyze and criticize one’s own technical skills and expressive performance skills appropriate to ballet dance level II.

rows.title: Choreography II
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate increased level of improvisational skills in the creative process of choreography and composition.
Express in written form the elements and creative process of choreography.
Apply more complex compositional skills to create choreography that reflects personal interpretation, imagination, and artistic values.
Analyze strengths and challenges as a choreographer and apply appropriate solutions.

rows.title: Dance Production IV
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Compose an original, intermediate-advanced level, full-length dance to be presented in a formal concert setting.
Instruct and direct one’s own full-length dance to student performers.
Use critical writing skills to analyze and evaluate one’s own original full-length dance.
Identify and complete production tasks that support a full-length concert performance.

rows.title: Dance Touring Ensemble IV
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Refine advanced technical skills and expressive performance skills of a full-length dance to be presented as a lecture-presentation and/or performed in a pre-professional setting.
Design a lesson plan for a dance lecture-presentation and formulate teaching strategies to co-instruct the lesson plan.
Use critical writing skills to analyze one’s own performance skills, teaching skills, and leadership role in a pre-professional dance ensemble.
Use critical writing skills to identify the components of managing a pre-professional dance ensemble.

rows.title: Modern Dance IV
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Memorize and identify Laban/Bartenieff vocabulary and modern dance vocabulary appropriate to level IV to recognize and interpret verbal and written instruction.
Demonstrate technical skills and expressive performance skills appropriate to modern dance level IV.
Use critical writing skills to analyze and criticize one’s own technical skills and expressive performance skills appropriate to modern dance level IV.
Use critical writing skills to complete personal critique and reflection of a dance concert performance.
Identify and discuss historical factors and present-day dance concepts that influence modern dance techniques.

rows.title: Jazz Dance IV
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Memorize and identify ballet and jazz dance vocabulary appropriate to level IV to recognize and interpret verbal and written instruction.
Demonstrate technical skills and expressive performance skills appropriate to jazz dance level IV.
Use critical writing skills to analyze and criticize one’s own technical skills and expressive performance skills appropriate to jazz dance level IV.
Use critical writing skills to complete personal critique and reflection of a jazz dance concert performance.
Discuss and interpret elements of dance composition appropriate to jazz dance level IV.

rows.title: Repertory IV
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate soft skills appropriate in the production of a dance concert.
Use critical writing skills to analyze one’s own technical and performance skills to improve a refinement of intermediate-advanced level performance roles assigned in guest and/or faculty repertory.
Execute a refinement of intermediate-advanced level technical skills and expressive performance to be performed in a formal concert setting,choreographed by faculty and/or guest choreographer.

rows.title: Somatic Practices in Dance
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Identify, analyze, and describe the major concepts and terminology of the Laban/Bartenieff System in class discussions and written assignments.
Apply Laban/Bartenieff principles and concepts to improve body connectivity and perform with clarity and efficiency their own developmental movement patterns.
Observe, analyze, and assess other student's movement patterns, based upon the Laban/Bartenieff system to improve their performance.

rows.title: Dance Practicum
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Present personal portfolio and identify and articulate objectives, goals, and work-related responsibilities specific to assigned dance internship.
Demonstrate, and continuously assess to improve, appropriate work-related skills specific to assigned dance internship.
Use critical writing skills to identify, analyze, and assess to improve, appropriate work-related skills specific to assigned dance internship.
Articulate and discuss final analysis of personal skill set and accomplishments specific to assigned dance internship.

rows.title: Special Studies in Jazz Dance
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Identify and apply anatomical fundamentals, and practical/theoretical concepts of ballet and jazz dance technique to analyze and criticize one’s own technical skills and expressive performance skills appropriate to advanced jazz dance technique.
Demonstrate advanced technical skills and expressive performance skills appropriate to jazz dance technique.
Use advanced writing skills to complete personal critique and reflection of a jazz dance concert performance.

rows.title: Exploration in the Field of Education
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Examine the roles and responsibilities of teachers in the classroom and educators outside the classroom.
Analyze teaching and learning of diverse student populations in traditional and non-traditional settings from early childhood to high school.
Identify educational terms and phrases.

rows.title: Introduction to Elementary Classroom Teaching
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Describe the rewards, complexities, and challenges in teaching.
Demonstrate how society’s influence impacts the teaching profession and differentiates today’s student population.
Compare and contrast the evolution of school and the traditional and educational schools of philosophy while formulating a personal educational philosophy.
Examine governance, ethics, and legal influences on the educational system.
Demonstrate understanding of curriculum, classroom management, assessment, and technology in the 21st Century classroom.

rows.title: Advanced Composition
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: develop effective thesis statements and demonstrate competency in the use of specific rhetorical patterns and logical patterns of development in well-organized paragraphs and essays
analyze methods of support in academic essays and use similar methods in writing
paraphrase and summarize effectively
use primary and secondary sources effectively in a documented paper

rows.title: Survey of the Bible as Literature
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Identify the major themes, motifs, archetypes, and recurrent images and characters in Biblical poetry, proverbs, prose, and prophecy.
Analyze Biblical literature from different critical perspectives and with regard to historical content and common literary conventions.
Produce college-level academic writing that demonstrates literal comprehension of texts, critical analysis, ethical use of primary and secondary sources, and correct MLA format and documentation.

rows.title: Shakespeare's Tragedies and History Plays
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Identify the major works, themes, subgenres, and dramatic conventions in the tragedy and history genres of Shakespearean drama.
Use different critical perspectives, as well as historical and cultural context, to analyze a selection of Shakespearean tragedies and histories.
Produce college-level academic writing that demonstrates literal comprehension of texts, critical analysis, ethical use of primary and secondary sources, and correct MLA format and documentation.

rows.title: The Modern American Novel
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: identify the major authors, works, themes, historical events, and literary conventions that have shaped American novels since 1900;
critically read a diverse selection of American novels and analyze each literary work from various critical perspectives;
produce college-level academic writing that demonstrates literal comprehension of texts, critical analysis, ethical use of primary and secondary sources, and correct MLA format and documentation.

rows.title: Survey of World Literature I
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: identify major authors, works, themes, historical events, and literary conventions in a variety of world literature from the Ancient world, the Medieval era, and the Early Modern Period;
consider form, content, literary conventions, and historical and cultural context to analyze literature from a variety of critical perspectives;
produce college-level academic writing that demonstrates literal comprehension of texts, critical analysis, ethical use of primary and secondary sources, and correct MLA format and documentation.

rows.title: Academic Reading and Writing
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: PART 2:
Demonstrate proficiency in summarizing, paraphrasing, and analyzing texts.
Demonstrate proficiency in supporting complex thesis statements with sufficient support.
Demonstrate proficiency in using standard written English.
Demonstrate proficiency in integrating and documenting appropriately chosen sources in MLA format (or when appropriate to the assignment APA format) in an academic research paper.

rows.title: Critical Thinking and Writing - Honors
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: PART 2:
Use knowledge of the components of argument, rhetorical devices, and logical fallacies to respond critically to various texts.
Be able to formulate sophisticated arguments and defend them with logical, persuasive evidence.
Demonstrate proficiency in using standard written English.

Demonstrate proficiency in integrating and documenting appropriately-chosen sources, both primary and secondary academic sources, in MLA format (or when appropriate APA format), in an academic research essay.
Demonstrate the ability to prepare and to present their original academic research in oral or poster presentation format. *(Honors)
Demonstrate the ability to distinguish between "Fake News/images" and reliable, legitimate sources. *(Honors)

rows.title: Introduction to Engineering
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge of strategies necessary to select and develop engineering careers.
Demonstrate ability to complete a project as part of a design team.

rows.title: Solidworks Advanced Solid Modeling
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Create three dimensional parametric solid models and assemblies using Solidworks software.
Create three dimensional parabolic shapes and apply advanced modules using Soildworks software.
Apply advanced computer skills with the use of Solidworks software.

rows.title: Advanced Plane Surveying
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
