rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: The student will be competent at demonstrating and leading a variety of group exercise activities.
The student will demonstrate verbal and nonverbal communication techniques used in small group and large group exercise settings.

rows.title: Legal Terminology
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Define basic legal terms and phrases in areas such as contracts, civil litigation, torts and criminal law.
Apply correct legal terms in approrpriate documents and settings.

rows.title: Mock Trial
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Evaluate courtroom procedures, legal strategies, and ethical considerations in trial practice.
Understand basic rules of evidence.
Prepare and deliver evidenciary testimony.

rows.title: Information Sources for Paraprofessionals: Tools and Techniques
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Identify the characteristics and organization of information.
Recognize types of reference sources and discuss their purposes.
Demonstrate proficiency in the use of basic and specialized reference and information retrieval tools.
Execute appropriate search techniques for the retrieval of information using online public catalogs, periodical databases, the internet, government documents, and the reference print collection.
Recognize standards for evaluating sources.
Identify reference services and information collections as they pertain to different libraries in different communities.

rows.title: Introduction to Digital Collections
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Describe basic concepts of digital collections, including the life cycle of digital assets, management systems, and the importance of metadata.
Describe the connection between metadata, usability, accessibility, and discoverability of digital materials.
Apply basic practices to manage digital collections, including planning, metadata, quality control, processing, and preservation to develop a small digital collection.
Demonstrate knowledge of different types of file formats, sizes, and proxies of digital materials for appropriate usage.
Demonstrate knowledge of copyright laws and principles relevant to digital collections, to make informed decisions about rights management and use.

rows.title: Work Experience - Medical Assistant
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: The work experience extern will perform professionally within the scope of practice of a medical assistant in a healthcare setting.
The work experience extern will competently perform administrative front office & / or clinical back office skills in a medical setting.
The work experience extern will create three work experience performance objectives to achieve successfully during rotation (Score between 6-9 points per performance objective to pass course).

rows.title: Advanced Medical Terminology
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: The student will report an increase in comprehension of medical terminology as it applies to the healthcare environment before the end of the term.
The student will evaluate the relationship of medical terminology to current events about research, diseases or innovations in healthcare before the end of the term.

rows.title: Computer Applications for the Medical Office
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: The student will utilize technology and demonstrate accurate use of medical practice management software by the end of the term.
The student will research a breach of Protected Health Information (PHI) related to Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) by the end of the term.

rows.title: Calculus for Biological, Management and Social Sciences
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Students will solve real-world application problems, distinguishing where to apply derivatives or integrals, and then formulate and communicate appropriate conclusions.

rows.title: Calculus I: Early Transcendentals – Embedded Support
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Evaluate limits and test functions for continuity, find derivatives and integrals of algebraic, trigonometric and other transcendental functions, and utilize derivatives and integrals in applications including extrema tests, related rates and finding areas.

rows.title: Quantitative Research Methods for Healthcare Professionals
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Students will be able to analyze journal articles and studies in the health sciences that utilize quantitative data.
Students will be able to formulate research questions, determine an effective plan for collecting data, and establish an experimental protocol for testing those questions.
Students will be able to determine if an experiment or study has sufficient evidence to determine statistical significance and/or causality.

rows.title: Principles of Management
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Communicate management principles to effect the behavior of others in the workplace.
Make sound management decisions based on different business scenarios.

rows.title: Introduction to Hospitality Management
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate effective and professional communication using industry specific language.
Describe methods for understanding and supporting multiculturalism in the workplace.

rows.title: Principles of Marketing
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Apply specific marketing information provided in the course to practical marketing scenarios using the four principles of marketing: product, price, promotion, and place
Identify marketing solutions by applying strategic and tactical marketing concepts to business and marketing problems.
Understand the concepts of Market Segementation, Targeting, and Positioning as it applies to marketing problems.

rows.title: Advertising and Distribution
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Delineate the fundamentals of advertising and promotion strategies by companies.
Plan and create promotional campaigns and how to use them to increase sales.
Define the functions of marketing channels of distribution and the operation of supply chains.

rows.title: Solidworks Beginning Solid Modeling
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate proper file management and computer skills related to Solidworks software
Create parametric solid model parts using Solidworks software
Create parametric solid model assemblies using Solidworks software

rows.title: Basic Mechanical Blueprint Reading
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Read and interpret views, dimensions, symbols, and annotations on mechanical blueprints

rows.title: QC Operations with PC-DMIS CMM-1
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Operate PC-DMIS software to inspect 3D parts based on parametric solid models.
Use PC-DMIS software to program and execute measurement routines.
Apply knowledge of PC-DMIS to generate inspection reports based on the inspections.

rows.title: Quality Control for Medical Devices
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Explain advanced aspects of Quality sytem regulation and International Standards Organization standard 13485.
Explain the priciples of six sigma and lean manufacturing as they relate to medical device manufacturing.
Demonstrate an understanding of quality tools, quality techniques and other aspects of organizational quality control as applied to medical device manufacturing.

rows.title: Technical Mathematics
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate basics of algebra, geometry, and trigonometry applicable to manufacturing processes.

rows.title: Conventional Machining Job Shop Skills
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Choose appropriate conventional manufacturing process to manufacture part ot mechanical drawing specifications.
Demonstrate use of grinders and saws at the intermediate level.
Choose approprite manufacturing technique to troubleshoot and manufacture parts from information other than mechanical drawings.

rows.title: Mastercam 3D Geometry, 3D Surfaces
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Create a 3D part geometry.
Compare the difference between 3D surfaces wireframe and 3D solid models.

rows.title: Advanced CNC Mill Programming, Set-up, and Operation
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Create a part program for four axis machine.
Select different tools and fixtures.
Set up and run a 4-axis CNC milling machine.

rows.title: Music Appreciation
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Describe Western classical musical characteristics, musical concepts, and specific contributions of important musicians using an appropriate musical terminology.

Write a music review of a live classical music performance that employs descriptive, interpretive and evaluative criticism of the performance as well as an effective use of an appropriate musical vocabulary.
Analyze the characteristics and context of music from different historical periods of Western classical music and distinguish between music of those different periods.

rows.title: Jazz in America
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Describe and analyze jazz musical characteristic, musical concepts, and specific contributions of important musicians from different stylistic periods of jazz using an appropriate jazz terminology.
Write a music review of a live jazz performance that employs descriptive, interpretive and evaluative criticism of the performance as well as an effective use of an appropriate musical vocabulary.
Express in written form, an assessment of the various cultural influences on jazz including race relations, the contributions of women, and social movements, in the United States.

rows.title: Music Fundamentals
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Analyze musical materials, of various musical cultures, in standard musical compositions relating to diatonic chord progression, phrase structure, key, intervallic content and expression markings using both musical analysis symbols and verbal explanations.

Create musical phrases illustrating principles of melodic and rhythmic construction synthesized from traditional “common practice” rules and analysis of literature, from various musical cultures, throughout history.
Perform simple rhythms, diatonic melodies, and triads by interpreting notation on the written score, from various musical cultures.
Solve musical problems in interval, triad and scale construction on keyboard, and on paper, using traditional principles of basic musical notation.

rows.title: Musicianship III
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Notate whole aural structures (melody, rhythm and chord progression) upon listening to dictated examples.
Perform sight singing examples that require the student to match theoretical concepts of diatonic and chromatic harmony musical sounds.
Distinguish discreet components of complex musical sounds, discern the relationship between them, and then name them.

rows.title: Applied Music (Private Instruction)
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Describe and evaluate style, elements of musicality, and technique as experienced in a live concert, using a vocabulary suitable to the musical genre.
Perform repertoire (more advanced than MUS 115B) and interpret it musically on their particular instrument.

Formulate a musical performance through accurate interpretation of more advanced scores (more advanced than MUS 115B) with correct performance practices appropriate to the musical genre relating to pitch, rhythm, tempo, balance & phrasing.

rows.title: Advanced Voice
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Define the terms and concepts associated with classical vocal technique.
Recognize classical vocal techniques in demonstrations and performances by other singers.
Perform in front of the class, demonstrating a level of vocal technique appropriate of an early advanced level singer.

rows.title: Chamber Choir
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Perform individual parts (S1,S2,A1,A2,T1,T2,B1,B2) by following the musical notation in the score and listening to the other members of the section.
Coordinate the singing of vocal part with that of the other choral parts by listening to the overall sound of the choir and following the direction of the conductor.
Perform with appropriate tone and expression based on the text, style, historical period, and aesthetic requirements of the music.

rows.title: Intermediate Techniques on the Digital Audio Workstation
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Design a plan of a musical project that incorporates the use and manipulation of more advanced MIDI tracks.
Produce original projects with musical ideas using the more advanced MIDI editing capabilities of the sequencing software.
Demonstrate advanced use of a variety of recording and editing techniques in a musical project.

rows.title: The Business of Music
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of standard business practices in the music industry by writing a report on a specific business topic.
Evaluate ethical issues of copyright law trademarks, fair practices and other legal concerns to determine how they apply to specific issues in the music business.
Analyze the career path of a prominent musical professional and present findings in an oral report.

rows.title: Class Piano II
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate their ability to play notes from assigned printed music, appropriate to advanced beginning level piano, using correct pitches, rhythm, appropriate dynamics, fingering, and a sense of creative expression.
Assess the musical effectiveness of a live piano performance by relating what they observe to basic aspects of piano performance methodology, in a written concert report.
Define the terms and concepts associated with advanced beginning level piano technique and musical notation.

rows.title: Stylistic Interpretation of Piano Repertoire
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: In a written concert report, assess the musical effectiveness of a live piano performance by relating what they observe to stylistic aspects of piano literature.
Apply specific stylistic elements from the Baroque, Classic, Romantic, and 20th/21st Century eras to compositions from those eras and then present those pieces in performance.
Recognize and identify specific elements of style appropriate to the various common practice and modern eras.

rows.title: Jazz Ensemble
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate in sound and time a realization of the jazz ensemble musical score appropriate to the musical genre, as well as demonstrate in performance a command of musical techniques related to rhythm, pitch, tuning, articulation, balance, and expressive interpretation.
Produce creative and artistic expression through rehearsal and performance of jazz ensemble literature.

rows.title: Intermediate String Methods
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate their ability to play notes from assigned printed music, appropriate to intermediate level strings, using correct pitches, rhythm, appropriate dynamics, fingering, and a sense of creative expression.
In a written concert report, assess the musical effectiveness of a live orchestral performance by relating what they observe to intermediate aspects of string performance methodology.
Define the terms and concepts associated with intermediate level string technique and musical notation.

rows.title: Advanced Classical Guitar
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate their ability to play notes from assigned printed music, appropriate to advanced level guitar, using correct pitches, rhythm, appropriate dynamics, fingering, and a sense of creative expression.
Assess the musical effectiveness of a live guitar performance by relating what they observe to advanced aspects of guitar performance methodology in a concert.
Define the terms and concepts associated with advanced level guitar technique and musical notation.

rows.title: Music Theory III
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Analyze musical materials in standard musical compositions relating to chromatic chord progression, form, four part-writing, non-harmonic tones and modulation techniques using both musical analysis symbols and verbal explanations.
Create musical examples illustrating principles of chromatic harmony synthesized from traditional “common practice” part writing rules and derived from analysis using a wide variety of literature.
Solve musical problems in chromatic part writing on keyboard and on paper using principles taught in lecture and textbook.

rows.title: Advanced Harmony and Composition II
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Discuss more advanced theoretical techniques of 20th and 21st century music, using an appropriate vocabulary.
Create assignments and compositional projects that illustrate technical and aesthetic concepts of 20th and 21st century compositional techniques covered in class.

rows.title: Symphonic Band
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate in sound and time a realization of the concert band musical score appropriate to the musical genre; they will demonstrate in performance a command of musical techniques related to rhythm, pitch, tuning, articulation, balance, and expressive interpretation.
Produce creative and artistic expression through rehearsal and performance of band literature.

rows.title: Family Health and Illness Concepts
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Communication: The student nurse will examine the application of communication skills to support decision making, education, and documentation of care related to family health and illness concepts.

Thinking & Reasoning: The student nurse will compare and contrast the nursing process and best current evidence to provide safe care related to family health and illness concepts while advocating for patients and families across the lifespan.
Information Management: The student nurse will examine technology to support decision making, education, and documentation of care related to family health and illness concepts.
Diversity: The student will examine individual responsibility, personal integrity, and respect for culturally diverse patient populations.
Civic Responsibility: The student nurse will examine responsibility for becoming informed, ethical and active nurses in their community.
Life Skills: The student nurse will examine interpersonal skills while providing safe care related to family health and illness concepts.
Careers: The student will evaluate accountability and responsibility for nursing practice, employing professionalism in the role of the Registered Nurse.

rows.title: Mental Health and Acute Concepts Lab
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Communication: The student nurse will integrate communication skills to support decision making, education, and documentation of care related to mental health and acute care concepts.

Thinking & Reasoning: The student nurse will integrate the application of the nursing process and best current evidence to provide safe care related to mental health and acute care concepts while advocating for patients and families across the lifespan.
Information Management: The student nurse will integrate technology to support decision making, education, and documentation of care related to mental health and acute care concepts.
Diversity: The student nurse will integrate individual responsibility, personal integrity, and respect for culturally diverse patient populations.
Civic Responsibility: The student nurse will integrate the responsibilities for becoming informed, ethical and active nurses in their community.
Life Skills: The student nurse will integrate the application of interpersonal skills while providing safe care related to mental health and acute concepts.
Careers: The student nurse will evaluate accountability and responsibility for nursing practice, employing professionalism in the role of the Registered Nurse.

rows.title: Food Safety and Sanitation
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Explain the roles of the food service worker and manager in the prevention of foodborne illnesses.

rows.title: Principles of Food Preparation
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Describe food safety and sanitation procedures.
Demonstrate basic knowledge of food preparation terminology and techniques.
Evaluate the sensory attributes of food.

rows.title: Movement Theory & Analysis
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Select theories of motor control to apply to clinical practice with a variety of client populations.
Compare motor learning and its application to recovery of function.
Evaluate the clinical management of postural control using motor, sensory, and cognitive processes of the client.
Design clinical treatment plans for clients with motor dysfunction based on evidence from research on motor control.

rows.title: Applying Research to Occupational Therapy Intervention
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Conclude the necessity for the Occupational Therapy Assistant (OTA) to provide evidence-based practice in Occupational Therapy.
Evaluate the skills to necessary in becoming an evidence-based practitioner.
Design a treatment protocol for a specific patient, population, or problem, including a literature review and analysis of evidence.

rows.title: Capstone Seminar
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Design an innovative solution to an identified therapeutic problem using the skills and knowledge developed through the program.
Analyze the effectiveness of their implemented projects.
Interpret the opinions of others through formal presentation of their project.

rows.title: Level II Fieldwork - Part II
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Implement interventions effectively to improve, maintain, develop and/or restore occupational performance skills.
Analyze clinical data and use clinical reasoning to make informed decisions to adapt or modify treatment plans.
Adhere to ethical and safety standards established by AOTA.

rows.title: Principles and Procedures in the Criminal Justice System
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Explain and evaluate legal concepts of due process within the criminal justice system.
Analyze and evaluate the stages and functions of the criminal justice trial process.

rows.title: Advanced Life Planning
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the procedures and documentation to assist an attorney in a probate and or elder law practice.

rows.title: Estate Planning and Administration
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate the skills necessary to assist an attorney in the planning and administration of estates.
Understand the probate and intestate sucesssion.

rows.title: Fundamentals of Labor Law
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Understand basic tenants of common law and statory labor law.
Identify labor issues in a legal hypothetical.

rows.title: Tort Law and Alternative Dispute Resolution
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Understand the paralegal's role in the law office regarding tort and alternate dispute resolution
Analyze hypothetical situations to spot issues for related torts.
Identify main types of alternate dispute resolution and their uses in litigation.

rows.title: Advanced Research and Writing
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of the court's analytical approach to law as applied to facts.
Apply logic while solving problems, explain their conclusions, and evaluate the analysis of others.
Utilize legal writing standards for citations, composition and mechanics.

rows.title: Advanced Technology in the Law Office
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Evaluate, redact, and log documents classified as privileged by attorney/client and work-product designations.
Explain industry standards for cyber security and encryption. Applications will be tested and their use demonstrated by students.

Demonstrate the ability to use on-premises and cloud computing technologies used by law offices will be reviewed and assessed considering confidentiality and privacy interests, functionality, and cost.

Apply advanced technology to assemble, review, check and finalize a legal brief, collect signatures, and electronically file the document. Evaluate different technology platforms to prepare legal notices, via electronic means.

rows.title: Advanced Legal Research, Analysis, and Writing
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Draft legal documents and papers using an appropriate analytical framework, proper style and format.

Formulate, execute, and evaluate complex search strategies using Boolean operators, advanced keyword selection, natural language queries, and other advanced search techniques to locate precise and relevant legal information including citations and Shepardizing.

Compare and contrast Legislative and Regulatory Research. Apply research techniques to track and analyze legislative changes and regulatory updates using public and private electronic sources to compare current law with legislative history.

Describe and design proper legal research utilizing a wide array of electronic resources available for legal research, including databases, online libraries, case law repositories, statutes, regulations, and international legal materials.

rows.title: Advanced Law Office Procedure, Transactions, and Forms
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Construct settlement letters and demand notices that clearly outline legal issues and state the terms and conditions for dispute resolution.
Develop templates for consumer notices and HIPAA notices that meet regulatory and statutory guidelines.
Justify the appropriate selection of judicial council forms and complete the forms accurately and in compliance with legal requirements.
Create a comprehensive client intake checklist to ensure accurate case assessment

rows.title: Introduction to Pharmacy Technology
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Describe the duties and roles of the pharmacy technician in various practice settings.
Identify the skills needed to successfully complete the Pharmacy Technology program at SAC.
Summarize the license and certification process for pharmacy technicians.
Differentiate drugs classified as OTC, Rx, (federal legend) C1, C2, C3, C4, C5.
Identify the steps involved in new drug development.
Discuss the characteristics of common drug dosage forms.
Memorize the 100 common trade-generic equivalents and indications.
Interpret prescriptions, memorize prescription sig codes, and prepare prescription labels.

rows.title: Inpatient Pharmacy Services
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate clear and concise communication of necessary information pertaining to written or verbal chart orders.
Use pharmacy calculations correctly to prepare chart orders.
Select common unit dose medications and supplies from the simulated pharmacy cabinets, to fill medication cassettes.
Analyze and interpret chart orders, transcribe chart orders into computer or manual profiles.
Demonstrate handling and preparing of medications in the inpatient pharmacy settings in a manner consistent with legal and ethical guidelines.
Analyze medication names and identify their medical indications.

rows.title: Pharmacy Technology Externship Outpatient
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge in Outpatient policies and procedures, medication filling, and patient safety.
Apply pharmacy class knowledge to ensure proper medication delivery to patients with all laws and required paperwork followed.

rows.title: Introduction to Philosophy
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate reflective philosophical engagement (personal growth) through deliberation that critically analyzes and evaluates philosophical concepts, issues, and/or perspectives.
Write effective essays that demonstrate knowledge of course material relevant to the thesis and analyze assigned material in a clear, systematic, original, thoughtful, and well-developed manner.
Use appropriate sources with sufficient interpretation and evaluation to develop coherent analysis or synthesis while properly citing relevant material.
Synthesize course-related material to evaluate the historical, social, and/or cultural development of concepts and their relation to issues faced by disparate communities.

rows.title: Honors Critical Thinking
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate reflective philosophical engagement (personal growth) through deliberation that critically analyzes and evaluates philosophical concepts, issues, and/or perspectives.
Write effective essays that demonstrate knowledge of course material relevant to the thesis and analyze assigned material in a clear, systematic, original, thoughtful, and well-developed manner.
Use appropriate sources with sufficient interpretation and evaluation to develop coherent analysis or synthesis while properly citing relevant material.
Identify the underlying rational structure of written sentences and arguments, as well as common reasoning errors and cognitive biases that lead to faulty argumentation.
Identify and analyze the logical structure of arguments.
Synthesize course-related material to evaluate the historical, social, and/or cultural development of concepts and their relation to issues faced by disparate communities.

rows.title: Photography Lab
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Produce technically competent digital photographs, applying fundamental level manual digital camera exposure and image control functions, according to current industry standards.
Demonstrate basic proficiency in contemporary digital photographic post-production and image editing techniques from camera to computer to printer using professional level tools.
Articulate and apply basic verbal (and/or written) critical analysis of photographic form, content and technique.

rows.title: Landscape Photography
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Produce technically competent digital landscape photographs by applying manual digital camera exposure and image control functions according to current industry standards.
Properly apply professional level digital camera lenses to landscape photographic compositions to manipulate light and depth of field.
Demonstrate intermediate-level application of contemporary digital photographic post-production and image editing techniques from camera to computer to printer using professional level tools.
Apply contemporary concepts in landscape photography, and articulate critical analysis of photographic form, content and technique.
Generate intentional, creative photographic content centered around a specific landscape theme and create a focused, dynamic, professionally presented portfolio.

rows.title: Commercial Photography
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Produce technically competent commercially-oriented photographs using manual digital camera exposure and image control functions according to current industry standards.
Properly apply contemporary camera lenses and lighting equipment to diverse commercial photographic projects in studio settings and on location.
Demonstrate proficiency in current digital photographic post-production and image editing techniques from camera to computer to printer using professional level tools.
Initiate commercial photography business practices including marketing, client agreements, image distribution guidelines and model releases.
Complete a creative digital portfolio of commercially-themed photographs, communicating an independent vision.

rows.title: Survey of General Physics
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Apply Newton’s laws of motion to solve problems involving forces and motion of physical bodies.
Analyze the behavior of fluids using concepts such as pressure, buoyancy, and the Ideal Gas Law.
Evaluate experimental data from lab experiments to draw conclusions about the principles of electricity, magnetism, and thermodynamics.
Describe the fundamental principles of wave motion and their applications in sound, light, and electromagnetic phenomena.

rows.title: Engineering Physics II
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Apply Coulomb’s law and Gauss’s law to solve problems involving electric fields and forces in systems with continuous and discrete charge distributions.
Analyze direct current (DC) and alternating current (AC) circuits using Kirchhoff’s laws, Ohm’s law, and the principles of capacitance and inductance.
Evaluate the effects of magnetic fields on moving charges and current-carrying wires, applying the Biot-Savart law and Ampère’s law to determine magnetic forces and fields.
Construct and explain the behavior of electromagnetic waves, using Maxwell’s equations to describe the relationship between electric and magnetic fields.

rows.title: American Government and Politics
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: PART 2:

Civic Participation - Students will demonstrate a general understanding of the American political system as well as the theoretical and operational design of American government institutions at the federal and state level.
Critical Thinking - Students will evaluate the democratic nature of American governmental institutions using standards of popular sovereignty, political equality, and liberty.

Diversity - Students will identify and explain contrasting views on the role of government, the virtues and vices of democratic decision making, and the balance of executive, legislative, and judicial power.

rows.title: Global Issues
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Civic Participation - Students will demonstrate a general understanding of major reoccurring and emerging global issues.
Critical Thinking - Students will identify various global issues and evaluate various policy solutions to the respective issues.
Diversity - Students will identify and explain the interconnectedness of various global issues and their varied impact on different regions throughout the world.

rows.title: Multicultural Psychology
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Explain concept of privilege and how it serves to define the worldviews of culturally diverse individuals.
Explain the concepts of ethnocentrism and cultural relativism and how these relate to understanding and biases toward individuals who are culturally different from us.
Articulate a broad understanding of the concept of culture.

rows.title: Introduction to Research Methods in Psychology
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate familiarity with major research method concepts, research designs, data analysis, and interpretation.
Demonstrate familiarity with writing formal scientific reports in American Psychological Association (APA) format.
Understand and apply research method principles and APA writing style in completing an independent research project.

rows.title: Psychopharmacology
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Explain, compare, and contrast drugs in the major drug classifications related to mechanisms of action, clinical (therapeutic) effects, side effects, uses, and abuses.
Demonstrate skills related to research report writing and adhering to APA standards.
Demonstrate an understanding of the course material through critical thinking and writing skills by completing written assignments, quizzes, and exams.
Recognize how different factors, such as gender, culture, age, and others, influence the choice and use of medications.
Describe the role of physiology in shaping and guiding our behaviors.
Explain how therapeutic drugs are developed through various stages of research, testing, and approval.
Discuss the ethical conduct of drugs studies using animal or human subjects.
Identify the types of research methods and designs used in pharmacology.
Identify and trace the historical development of behavioral pharmacology as a scientific discipline.

rows.title: Introduction to Psychology - Honors
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: PART 2:
Compare and contrast major theoretical perspectives of psychology and explain how to apply these perspectives to personal and professional life.
Describe the scientific process within psychological research, the APA standards for writing, the major ethical guidelines, and the impact of diversity on psychological research.
Explain human behavior as a function of biological, cognitive, and socio-cultural factors.

rows.title: Honors Introduction to Sociology
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Students will identify and apply the main sociological theoretical frameworks to analyze social stratification based on race, ethnicity, gender, social class, sexuality or other social groups.
Students will apply sociological research to distinguish the interrelatedness of various social intuitions.
Students will identify the role of culture and socialization in the development of one’s beliefs, opinions, and values.

rows.title: Intro to Race and Ethnicity
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Explain how race and ethnicity are a social construction.
Distinghish between race and ethnicity in contemporary society.
Analyze and explain the consequences of racism in contemporary society.

rows.title: Elementary Spanish I
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Write basic descriptive paragraphs in Spanish with clear topic sentences and supporting detail.
Read, analyze, and express personal opinions in Spanish on a diverse set of cultural topics.
Use appropriate grammatical structures that include beginning-level vocabulary and verb conjugations.
Engage in oral discussion by actively listening and speaking on a variety of topics.

rows.title: Advanced Conversational Spanish
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Understand main ideas and most details of connected discourse on a variety of topics beyond the immediacy of the situation.
Build vocabulary and expand the use of more advanced grammatical structures.
Communicate effectively in spoken-Spanish using different types of discourse at the intermediate-advanced level.
Understand and discuss a wide range of written texts (both fiction and nonfiction).

rows.title: Intermediate Spanish II
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Write multiple compositions in Spanish at the intermediate level using description, summary, comparisons, and other modes.
Demonstrate understanding of critical analysis of literary material.
Express personal opinions and perspectives in Spanish on specific readings.
Engage in oral discussions by actively listening and speaking on topics related to cultural aspects of the Spanish-speaking world.

rows.title: Introduction to Statistics
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: PART 2:
Correctly interpret a graphical display of data.
Take a statistical claim about a data set, perform an appropriate procedure, and write a conclusion that addresses that claim.

rows.title: Theatre History 1
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Evaluate historical periods and plays.
Interpret the worldview presented by the playwrights in each play to learn about the phenomenon of theatre in different cultural epochs.
Understand the historical development of theatre from the Greek period through the 17th century.

rows.title: Acting for the Camera
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate imagination and personal interpretation in the development of an original character scenario for the screen.
Apply knowledge of the aesthetic reality involved in acting for the camera by comparing and contrasting technical performance techniques.
Utilize practical methodologies involving the technical approach required to create a fully realized performance for the camera.

rows.title: Musical Theatre History
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Connect the modern musical with its musical antecedents in Europe and America.
Analyze text and musical structure in a musical play.
Critique the use of dance and varying performance styles of live and filmed musicals.

rows.title: Stagecraft
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Use the elements of design in the development of aesthetic decisions.
Compare the three scenic designer drawing types: ground plan, elevation, perspectives.
Identify the cultural influences and physical features of Ancient Greek, Roman, Elizabethan, and Italian Renaissance theatre architecture.

rows.title: Introduction to Stage Costume
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Analyze a play script to assess both character and costuming needs.
Create costume design concepts.
Integrate historical research methods in the creation of costume designs.

rows.title: Rehearsal and Performance in Production
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Evaluate and analyze a script for rehearsal and performance.
Demonstrate a strong work ethic within a professional framework of collaboration.
Create and dramatize the behavioral life of a character in rehearsal and performance.

rows.title: Introduction to Directing
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Develop an analysis of the dramatic action, the characters, and the dialogue.
Coach actors during rehearsals and effectively communicate their production concept to the design team.
Demonstrate practical experience in leadership and personnel management recognizing the essential skills for success in this role.

rows.title: Fundamentals of Programming
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Utilize imagination in the development of design solutions.
Determine the proper method of controlling the available attributes for automated lighting instruments.
Correct attribute problems within a specific type of instrument.

rows.title: Musical Theatre Workshop
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate appearance, personality, character, focus, pitch, clarity, diction, projection and final beat in performance.
Utilize character objectives, obstacles and tactics when developing character choices.
Apply dramatic and musical terminology and procedures during rehearsals and performance.

rows.title: Improvisation for Stage and Screen
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Discover and define style as it applies to period and contemporary stage plays.
Utilize interactive listening strategies as it pertains to the use of stylized theatrical language and comedic timing.
Use imagination and personal interpretation in the development of multiple dramatic characters.

rows.title: Introduction to Preventative Maintenance Inspection
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Apply proper safety procedures when working on medium/heavy duty vehicles.
Indentify engine, air induction and fuel system in need of maintenance.
Inspect brake components of a medium/heavy-duty vehicle for both air and hydraulic brakes to meet CHP and DOT criteria.
Identify high-voltage components for electric heavy-duty vehicles.

rows.title: Introduction to Hybrid/Electric Vehicles
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate safe practices and procedures when working with/on high voltage electric vehicles.
Construct electrical circuits and components to create an operational hybrid/electric vehicle.
Explain battery balancing and the operation of an electrical inverter.
Explain regenerative braking found on hybrid and electric vehicles.

rows.title: Introduction to Keyboarding I
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Key a minimum of 28 words per minute with no more than 5 errors in a 2-minute timing.
Demonstrate proper typing posture and the ability to key using proper finger and hand placement.

rows.title: Introduction to Microsoft Access
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Describe the difference between a database and spreadsheet application, such as MS Excel, and the benefits and limitations of each.
Design and develop tables, queries, forms, and reports.
Create a database and demonstrate the ability to enter, edit, delete, sort and filter data within it.

rows.title: Introduction to Microsoft Word
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Use templates to create professionally designed documents, such as letters, reports, business cards, cover letter, or resume.
Create, edit, format, save, and print documents.
Distinguish the difference between "Save" and "Save As" functions and use "Save As" to save to a particular folder and name the document.

rows.title: Introduction to Quickbooks
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Create invoices.
Enter payments, deposits, and pay bills.
Add, edit, and inactivate customers.

rows.title: MS PowerPoint
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Create and edit a PowerPoint presentation utilizing text and images.
Format slide backgrounds or apply template designs to existing slides.
Save, package, and output finished presentations for delivery.
Print slides, handouts, and notes.

rows.title: Certified Human Resources Professional (SHRM-CP) Exam Preparation & Practice
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Take the latest SHRM Certified Professional (SHRM-CP) certification exam and continue your career pathway in human resources.
List the nine key behavioral competencies and 14 HR functional areas.

rows.title: Basic Computer Repair & COMPTIA A+ Certification Preparation
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Prepare to take the latest A+ certification exams.

rows.title: Digital Literacy for Real World Application – Tier 4
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Discern the impact of one's digital footprint.
Evaluate content found online.
Develop a professional portfolio online.
Employ formatting and design standards to create an online and traditional resume.

rows.title: Introduction to How to Start a Small Business
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Identify potential customers and the proper marketing strategy to use.
Write a draft of their business plan.
Identify the most appropriate business structure for their business.

rows.title: Web Design
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Explain the cultural impact of internet technology in a global, regional, and local context.
Identify and explain issues of equity related to internet access, information access, and technological access on a global, regional and local level.
Clarify, examine, and debate legal issues of governance, rights, and ethics related to the internet utilizing various perspectives.
Use industry-accepted tools and strategies for site map and experience design development.
Use basic HTML authoring and code snippets to solve web design problems.
Identify proper web developer tools for a variety of client-driven outcomes.

rows.title: Beginning Sewing
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate samples of various seam finishes, edge finishes, excess fabric construction techniques, and closure applications.
Reconstruct a lined garment.

rows.title: Baking & Pastry Basics
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Correctly use basic baking and pastry equipment and tools.
List and discuss correct selection and utilization of baking and pastry supplies and ingredients.
List and apply the skills involved in the mixing, production, and finishing of a variety of basic pastry products.
List and discuss qualities and standards for contemporary restaurant plated desserts.
List, discuss, and apply the standards for sanitary product use and storage of items produced in the baking and pastry class.

rows.title: Dance Laboratory II
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Apply critical analysis of performance skills.
Memorize and demonstrate technical and performance dance skills necessary for beginning-intermediate level dance projects.

rows.title: Technical Production
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Execute duties as directed within your assigned technical discipline.
Utilize concepts learned in the production build process to execute assigned technical responsibilities.
Serve as a member of the technical team working on a production.

rows.title: Tour Ensemble
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Develop character analyses and biographies.
Score dialogue and character arc in a script.
Value clear pronunciation, articulation skills, and appropriate vocal techniques in performance.

rows.title: Modern Dance I
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Memorize and identify ballet and modern dance vocabulary appropriate to level I to recognize and interpret verbal and written instruction.
Demonstrate technical skills and expressive performance skills appropriate to modern dance level I.
Use critical writing skills to analyze and criticize one’s own technical skills and expressive performance skills appropriate to modern dance level I.
Use critical writing skills to complete personal critique and reflection of a modern dance concert performance.
Identify and discuss historical factors and present-day dance concepts that influence modern dance techniques.

rows.title: Repertory I
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate soft skills appropriate in the production of a dance concert.
Use critical writing skills to analyze one’s own technical and performance skills to improve beginning level performance roles assigned in guest and/or faculty repertory.
Execute beginning level technical skills and expressive performance to be performed in a formal concert setting choreographed by faculty and/or guest choreographer.

rows.title: Motion Picture Performance Production
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Evaluate a script for performance.
Support the behavioral life of a character for the camera in performance.
Demonstrate a strong work ethic within a professional framework of collaboration.

rows.title: Certified Nursing Assistant (CNA) Training- Clinical
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Identify the roles and responsibilities of a CNA.
Apply effective interpersonal communication skills for basic nursing care, and a positive working relationship with all members of the healthcare team, residents and their families.
Implement safe and competent resident care.
Identify standard precautions and basic principles related to infection prevention.
Identify metric system, weights, and military time.
Execute the care for patients including bathing, dressing, overall hygiene, feeding and toileting.
Perform vital signs correctly.
Recognize and report patient abuse.

rows.title: Acute Care Nursing Assistant Clinical
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Describe and implement proper care for patients in an acute care setting.
Exhibit proficient communication, interpersonal, and documentation abilities to enhance patient care.
Collaborate with licensed nursing staff to assess and monitor patients in an acute care setting, providing valuable support in the healthcare team.

rows.title: Introduction to Mental Health Disorders
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Identify at least four (4) mental health disorders.
Describe the most common symptoms of at least four (4) mental health disorders.
Identify at least one (1) treatment option for four (4) mental health disorders.

rows.title: Introduction to Pharmacy Technology
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Describe the duties and roles of the pharmacy technician are in various practice settings.
Identify the skills you need to successfully complete the Pharmacy Technology program at SAC.
Summarize the license and certification process for pharmacy technicians.
Differentiate drugs classified as OTC, Rx, (federal legend) C1, C2, C3, C4, C5.
Identify the steps involved in new drug development.
Discuss the characteristics of common drug dosage forms.
Memorize the 100 common trade-generic equivalents and indications.
Interpret prescriptions, memorize prescription sig codes, and prepare prescription labels.

rows.title: Basic Machining Concepts and Operations
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate use of conventional milling machine at the basic level.
Demonstrate use of conventional lathe machine at the basic level.
Analyze mechanical drawings and choose appropriate manufacturing processes.

rows.title: Math/Blueprint Reading for Welders
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Identify common blueprint welding symbols.
Interpret information given on blueprints.
Define key views used in blueprints.
Calculate mathematical problems used in welding.

rows.title: Advanced Electric Arc Welding
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate safety standards and rules given in this course that apply to welding equipment, work habits, and industrial environment.
Identify chemical composition for filler wire and electrodes.
Sketch advanced welding symbols for structural joints.

rows.title: Welding Certification D1.1 Code Clinic
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Use the AWS D1.1 code book index to locate specific code information.
Apply an understanding on how to read prequalified procedures.
Demonstrate the ability to read figures and tables.

rows.title: Money, Sex, and Power
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Identify historical and contemporary events and legislation affecting women's paid and unpaid labor.

Employ an intersectional lens to analyze obstacles such as sexual harassment, child care, and the “glass ceiling," globalization, and unpaid labor as situated within a socio-political context affecting women.
